Messages.Author: Ken Mikolaj
Messages.Body:
Since FD is an action modifier, can it be played any time during the action?

Can it be played after combat?

Can it be played after combat by a Vamp in Torpor?

Thanks

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Ken Mikolaj <ke...@eden.com> writes:
>Since FD is an action modifier, can it be played any time during the action?

No - card text allows it to be played only once the action is successful,
or (in superior) once the action is blocked.

>Can it be played after combat?

Yes, if the combat was the action (i.e., Bum's Rush).

A combat resulting from a blocked action is not part of the action -
that combat takes place after the action (so Freak Drive would have
to be played before the combat).

>Can it be played after combat by a Vamp in Torpor?

Yes, under the terms above (in Torpor after a Rush combat).

In article <Pine.BSD/.3.91.9612091623...@matrix.eden.com>,

Ken Mikolaj <ke...@eden.com> writes
>Since FD is an action modifier, can it be played any time during the action?
>

>Can it be played after combat?
>

>Can it be played after combat by a Vamp in Torpor?
>

>Thanks

The card says that the action can only be played by a vampire that is
not blocked (at basic level) or blocked (superior level) and is played
immediately after the action is performed.

If your combat was from a Bum's Rush then after it if it wasn't blocked
(normal level), or even if it was blocked (or another action was
blocked) at superior.

In both cases I would say that you should play it after the blocking (or
not blocking) but before combat begins.

Shouldn't be playable by vampires in torpor because they can't do much.
They are specifically noted on cards if they can (eg Movement of the
Slow Body from Jyhad set)
--
Justin

Not a good argument. "They can't do much" means little in terms of game

[Re: Freak Drive]
> Shouldn't be playable by vampires in torpor because they can't do much.
> They are specifically noted on cards if they can (eg Movement of the
> Slow Body from Jyhad set)

Since they are not prohibited from playing action modifiers, vampires
who have just entered torpor would be allowed to play a Freak Drive,
if they still had the blood.

Conversly, Reaction cards such as Cat's Guidance are played after the
block is successfull but before combat begins. This may be the last
chance to play action modifiers on the action.

Don't really know what the RULE is.

That timing rule applies to action modifiers as well.
If you are blocked, you must play (superio) Freak Drive before the
resulting combat, or not play it at all.

If you are unblocked (in the case of Bum's Rush, et. al.), you can
play the Freak Drive (inferior) after the action (combat) is
completed, as normal (even if you are in torpor at that time).

Similarly, you can play Freak Drive (inferior) after other successful
actions that result in the acting vampire going to torpor: Force
of Will, an action modifier by Day Operation, etc.
